    Network meta-analysis

    Source: R/meta-network.R
    meta_network.Rd

    meta_network() fits a frequentist, contrast-based network meta-analysis by generalised least squares (Lu and Ades, 2006; Rucker, 2012). Each study contributes the contrasts of its arms against a study baseline. For studies with more than two arms, the arm level variances are reconstructed from the pairwise variances (Rucker and Schwarzer, 2014), so the within-study covariance is respected. Random effects share one between-study variance \(\tau^2\) under the consistency assumption, with covariance \(\tau^2/2\) between contrasts of the same multi-arm study, and \(\tau^2\) is estimated by restricted maximum likelihood.

    Usage

    meta_network(
  .data,
  study,
  treat1,
  treat2,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  reference = NULL,
  method = "REML",
  level = 0.95,
  small_values = c("good", "bad")
)

    Arguments

    .data

    Contrast level data with one row per pairwise comparison, such as the output of meta_pairwise().

    study, treat1, treat2

    <data-masking> Columns identifying the study and the two treatments compared. The effect size is that of treat1 relative to treat2.

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    reference

    The reference treatment. Defaults to the most connected treatment.

    method

    "REML" (random effects) or "FE" (common effect).

    level

    Confidence level.

    small_values

    Are small (negative) effect sizes "good" (for example fewer adverse events) or "bad" (for example fewer people who quit smoking)? Used for the P-scores.

    Value

    A <meta_nma> with one row per treatment: the effect relative to the reference, its confidence interval and the P-score. Use tidy() for the league table, inconsistency decomposition and direct and indirect split.

    Details

    Treatments are ranked by P-scores (Rucker and Schwarzer, 2015), the frequentist analogue of the surface under the cumulative ranking curve. Global inconsistency is assessed by decomposing the common-effect Q statistic into within-design heterogeneity and between-design inconsistency (Krahn, Binder and Konig, 2013). Local inconsistency is assessed for each comparison with direct evidence by contrasting the direct estimate with the indirect estimate obtained by back-calculation (Dias et al., 2010). The direct estimates pool every contrast that compares the pair, so for multi-arm studies the split is approximate.

    References

    Lu, G. and Ades, A. E. (2006). Assessing evidence inconsistency in mixed treatment comparisons. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 101(474), 447-459. doi:10.1198/016214505000001302

    Rucker, G. (2012). Network meta-analysis, electrical networks and graph theory. Research Synthesis Methods, 3(4), 312-324. doi:10.1002/jrsm.1058

    Rucker, G. and Schwarzer, G. (2014). Reduce dimension or reduce weights? Comparing two approaches to multi-arm studies in network meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine, 33(25), 4353-4369. doi:10.1002/sim.6236

    Rucker, G. and Schwarzer, G. (2015). Ranking treatments in frequentist network meta-analysis works without resampling methods. BMC Medical Research Methodology, 15, 58. doi:10.1186/s12874-015-0060-8

    Krahn, U., Binder, H. and Konig, J. (2013). A graphical tool for locating inconsistency in network meta-analyses. BMC Medical Research Methodology, 13, 35. doi:10.1186/1471-2288-13-35

    Dias, S., Welton, N. J., Caldwell, D. M. and Ades, A. E. (2010). Checking consistency in mixed treatment comparison meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine, 29(7-8), 932-944. doi:10.1002/sim.3767

    Examples

    pw <- meta_pairwise(smoking_cessation, study = study, treatment = trt,
  measure = "OR", event = xi, n = ni)
nma <- meta_network(pw, study = study, treat1 = treat1, treat2 = treat2,
  reference = "no_contact", small_values = "bad")
nma
#> # Network meta-analysis <meta_nma>
#> # Model: random effects, restricted maximum likelihood; reference: no_contact
#> # Measure: log odds ratio; 24 studies, 4 treatments, 8 designs
#> # tau^2 = 0.4502; Q(23) = 202.62, p < 0.0001
#> # Inconsistency between designs: Q(7) = 15.22, p = 0.0333
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   treatment      estimate std.error conf.low conf.high pscore
#>   <chr>             <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 no_contact        0        NA       NA         NA    0.0411
#> 2 grp_counseling    0.869     0.372    0.139      1.60 0.847 
#> 3 ind_counseling    0.709     0.195    0.326      1.09 0.716 
#> 4 self_help         0.397     0.329   -0.247      1.04 0.396 
tidy(nma, type = "league")
#> # A tibble: 12 × 8
#>    treat1         treat2 estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high
#>    <chr>          <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 grp_counseling no_co…    0.869     0.372     2.33  1.96e-2    0.139     1.60 
#>  2 ind_counseling no_co…    0.709     0.195     3.63  2.82e-4    0.326     1.09 
#>  3 self_help      no_co…    0.397     0.329     1.21  2.27e-1   -0.247     1.04 
#>  4 no_contact     grp_c…   -0.869     0.372    -2.33  1.96e-2   -1.60     -0.139
#>  5 ind_counseling grp_c…   -0.160     0.353    -0.452 6.51e-1   -0.852     0.533
#>  6 self_help      grp_c…   -0.472     0.405    -1.16  2.45e-1   -1.27      0.323
#>  7 no_contact     ind_c…   -0.709     0.195    -3.63  2.82e-4   -1.09     -0.326
#>  8 grp_counseling ind_c…    0.160     0.353     0.452 6.51e-1   -0.533     0.852
#>  9 self_help      ind_c…   -0.312     0.339    -0.920 3.58e-1   -0.976     0.353
#> 10 no_contact     self_…   -0.397     0.329    -1.21  2.27e-1   -1.04      0.247
#> 11 grp_counseling self_…    0.472     0.405     1.16  2.45e-1   -0.323     1.27 
#> 12 ind_counseling self_…    0.312     0.339     0.920 3.58e-1   -0.353     0.976
tidy(nma, type = "inconsistency")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   source              Q    df  p.value
#>   <chr>           <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 total           203.     23 1.08e-30
#> 2 within designs  187.     16 2.75e-31
